    ⛵ حضارتا ماجان ودلمون

    The ancient civilisations of Magan and Dilmun

    The big idea: about 4,000 years ago, two trading civilisations lived around the Arabian Gulf. Magan was on the southern coast of the Gulf, where the UAE and Oman are today. Dilmun was in the east of the Arabian Peninsula, where Bahrain is today. Both traded with Mesopotamia (بلاد الرافدين, today's Iraq).

    👆 Tap a pin on the map.

    Simplified map, not to scale.

    🔤 ماذا تعني الأسماء؟ What do the names mean?

    ماجان

    In the old Sumerian language (السومرية), ما (ma) means ship and جان (gan) means hull / frame. So Magan is linked to ship-building: they were great sailors!

    دلمون

    🌊🌊🌊🌊🏝️

    سُمّيت دلمون بهذا الاسم لأنها تُحاط بالمياه من جميع النواحي الأربع.

    Dilmun got its name because it is surrounded by water on all four sides: it is an island (Bahrain).

    ⚒️ النشاط الاقتصادي Jobs people did (economic activities)

    Count them! Magan had 4 jobs: industry, farming, hunting and trade. Dilmun had 3 jobs: farming, industry and fishing. (This is a question in the school form!)

    🤝 العادات والتقاليد والسنع

    Customs, traditions and "Sanaa" (good manners)

    Customs and traditions (العادات والتقاليد) are everything we receive from our grandparents, parents, teachers and community: habits, knowledge and ways of doing things.
    Why are they important? They shape who we are, and they help us tell people apart by where they come from.
    السنع (Sanaa) is the set of Emirati rules for how we behave with people every day: respecting elders, courage, sincerity, generosity, honesty and hospitality.

    📜 التراث الثقافي وأقسامه

    Cultural heritage and its three parts

    Cultural heritage (التراث الثقافي) is everything passed from one generation to the next: customs, knowledge, manners and arts. Your sheet splits it into 3 parts: folk proverbs (الأمثال الشعبية), bedtime stories (الخروفة) and folk chants / songs (الأهازيج الشعبية).
    💡 In Emirati dialect, ي often replaces ج: يارك = جارك (your neighbour), يلي = اللي (the one who), يبي = يريد (wants).

    🇦🇪 يوم الشهيد

    Martyrs' Day (Commemoration Day), 30 November

    Martyrs' Day is a national day the UAE marks every 30 November to honour the sacrifices of its martyrs. The first Emirati martyr was Salem Suhail Khamis from Ras Al Khaimah. He joined the police at only 16, and he was martyred on Greater Tunb island on 30 November 1971, just two days before the UAE was founded (2 December 1971).
